name: Give an independent risk view on proposed transactions (one transaction reviewed)
summary: Before the Portfolio Execution Committee decides on a new private investment, follow-on, fund commitment, manager engagement or exit, the Risk group, independent of the investment departments, gives the committee its own view of what the deal adds to the fund's market, credit, liquidity, leverage and concentration risk. A principal triages each memo; for most new deals an associate and senior associate question the deal team, measure the deal's contribution to potential loss and limits, judge the downside case and draft an opinion that a principal and director approve, while routine items get a one-page note. The work runs on the deal team's bid timetable, so it is squeezed by late memos, slow answers to questions and deal terms that change after the opinion is written.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager with about 2,000 employees investing most private assets directly through internal teams, with a second-line Risk group reporting to the CFRO.
baseline.notes: Modelled on the governance the model fund describes for fiscal 2020 to 2022 (ISRC, PEC and IRC). Department risk teams for private equity, real assets and credit sit in Investment risk oversight.

trigger: A deal team or the committee secretariat sends Risk a draft investment memo or exit proposal that will go to the Portfolio Execution Committee.
end_state: An approved risk opinion or short-form note is in the committee package and the Head of Risk is briefed, or the deal is withdrawn before the opinion is finished.

volume.seasonality: Fairly even through the year with peaks before calendar year end and around large auction deadlines.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's process map (30 to 65 a month) and matching the committee workflow's 35 to 60 items a month; based on about 20 closings a month across departments plus commitments, follow-ons and exits.

Org file role. About 180 minutes a case for intake, triage, reviews and the deal team check over 45 cases a month; Job Bank shows market wages for the occupation, the org file's higher cost includes incentive pay.
Org file role. About 320 minutes a case including short-form notes.
Org file role. About 615 minutes a case on average including rework and updates, the analytical core of each opinion.
Org file role. Approval and briefing, about 70 minutes a case.
Org file role. Escalated opinions only, about one in twelve cases.
Org file role, added to stand in for deal team members of all investment departments who answer Risk's questions; about 90 minutes on each full review.

steps.name: Log the request and assign a reviewer
steps.description: A Risk principal receives the draft investment memo, model and term sheet from the deal team or the committee secretariat, logs it in the transaction tracker with the target committee date and any bid deadline, and assigns the associate and senior associate who cover that department.

evidence.note: Risk gives independent challenge and formal guidance to approval bodies; tracker and assignment by department coverage are estimates.

steps.name: Decide the depth of review
steps.description: The principal compares the deal size, type and risk with the Risk Policy thresholds and recent opinions: new direct investments, large commitments and leveraged or concentrated deals get a full opinion, while small follow-ons, routine fund commitments and most exits get a short-form note.

error.defect_description: A deal that needs a full review is routed to the short-form path.

control.basis: Risk Policy and management authorities: independent risk guidance required for transactions going to the Portfolio Execution Committee

evidence.note: Formal guidance is required on certain matters (F2021); the 63/37 split between full and short-form reviews is an estimate.

steps.name: Read the memo and model and list questions
steps.description: The Risk associate reads the memo, the base and downside cases in the model, the capital structure, the partner and governance terms and the diligence findings, and writes a list of questions on assumptions, leverage, exit routes and data gaps.

error.defect_description: A material assumption or structural feature is not questioned.

evidence.note: Review content follows the risk types the F2022 report lists (market, credit, liquidity, leverage); hours are estimates.

steps.name: Send questions and chase the deal team
steps.description: The associate emails the question list to the deal team's senior associate, agrees a time to walk through the model, and follows up when answers are late against the committee date.

evidence.note: Question and chase cycle is common practice; effort estimated.

steps.name: Deal team answers the risk questions
steps.description: A deal team senior associate pulls answers from the model, the data room and advisers' reports, adds sensitivity runs where asked, and replies to Risk; deal work for the bid usually takes priority, so answers queue.

error.defect_description: Answer based on an outdated model version.

next.condition: deal dropped or lost before the opinion

evidence.note: Round 2 of an auction lasts 4 to 6 weeks, so deal teams answer under bid pressure. Private equity senior associate stands in for deal teams from all departments; the 4% withdrawal share matches the 3% to 5% of items withdrawn in the committee workflow (estimate).

steps.name: Pull current exposures and limit headroom
steps.description: The associate pulls from the risk platform the department's risk budget use, its contribution to total fund potential loss, and existing exposure to the same company, sector, country and currency across all departments, and checks the deal against the 10% single-entity limit and the leverage and liquidity limits.

error.defect_description: An existing exposure held through another department or a fund is missed.

control.basis: The model fund Regulations s. 11(1): no more than 10% of book value of assets in one person or associated persons; s. 13(1) 30% voting limit

evidence.note: Regulatory limits from SOR/99-190; department potential loss contributions reported in F2022. Check by Risk rather than Compliance alone is an assumption.

steps.name: Run incremental risk and stress analysis
steps.description: A senior associate maps the deal to proxy risk factors, runs its incremental contribution to one-year potential loss and to the department's risk budget, applies the standard stress scenarios and credit loss measures, and records the non-recourse leverage and unfunded commitments it adds.

error.defect_description: Wrong proxy mapping understates the deal's risk contribution.

evidence.note: Potential loss, stress scenarios, permanent loss and leverage measures described in F2022 and F2020; incremental analysis per deal and hours are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm funding and liquidity impact with Total Fund Management
steps.description: For large deals the senior associate asks the liquidity and collateral principal whether funding the deal, its unfunded commitments and any guarantees keep the liquidity coverage and leverage within limits over the forecast horizon, and records the answer.

control.basis: Investment Statement s. 9.5: Board-approved liquidity and leverage limits

evidence.note: Liquidity and leverage limits (Investment Statement s. 9.5; F2022 leverage limit 45%). Consultation threshold and share estimated.

steps.name: Assess deal-specific risks and the downside case
steps.description: The senior associate judges the deal's own risks: leverage and covenant headroom at the asset, sensitivity of returns to key assumptions, exit and liquidity risk, partner and governance protections, currency, and climate or ESG flags raised in diligence, and compares them with similar past deals.

error.defect_description: Downside case accepted from the deal team without independent challenge.

evidence.note: Risk independently challenges the first line's assessment of risks (F2022). Hours estimated.

steps.name: Draft the risk opinion
steps.description: The senior associate writes a two to four page opinion: an overall view (supportive, supportive with conditions, or not supportive), the main risks and mitigants, the effect on department and total fund limits, and recommended conditions such as leverage caps or monitoring triggers.

error.defect_description: Opinion text and the figures in its tables disagree.

evidence.note: Opinion format and length are estimates based on common practice for second-line transaction opinions.

steps.name: Principal reviews the draft opinion
steps.description: The principal checks the analysis and proxies, challenges the conclusions and wording, and either clears the draft or returns it with comments.

error.defect_description: A proxy or stress error is not caught.

control.basis: Four-eyes review within Risk: the reviewer is not the drafter

evidence.note: Four-eyes review is common practice; return rate estimated.

steps.name: Share the draft with the deal team for a factual check
steps.description: The principal sends the draft to the deal team lead or walks it through on a call so factual errors are corrected before committee; if the deal team changes price, structure or leverage in response, Risk reassesses.

evidence.note: Factual check with the first line is common practice; share of material changes estimated.

steps.name: Director approves the risk opinion
steps.description: The Risk director responsible for the department reads the opinion and its support, confirms the overall view and conditions, and approves it for the committee or sends it back; contested or limit-breaching views go to the Head of Risk.

control.basis: Risk Policy: second-line opinion approved at director level before submission to the Portfolio Execution Committee

next.condition: not supportive, contested or limit impact

evidence.note: Risk reports to the CFRO and gives formal guidance to committees; approval level and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Escalate the opinion to the Head of Risk
steps.description: The Managing Director, Head of Risk reviews opinions that are not supportive, take a department or total fund limit close to its threshold, or go to the Board committee, discusses them with the department head if needed and signs the final view.

control.basis: Risk Policy escalation of significant risk views; Investment Statement s. 9.9 Board-level transactions

evidence.note: Transactions above Board limits go to the Investment Strategy Committee (s. 9.9, terms of reference). Escalation criteria and shares estimated.

steps.name: Prepare a short-form risk note
steps.description: For routine items the associate pulls the exposure and limit headroom summary, notes any concentration or leverage effect and writes a one-page note confirming the item is within limits and naming any points for the committee.

error.defect_description: Exposure held elsewhere in the fund is missed.

evidence.note: Short-form treatment of routine follow-ons, fund commitments and exits is an estimate.

steps.name: Principal signs the short-form note
steps.description: The principal checks the note against the memo and the exposure summary and signs it, returns it for correction, or upgrades the item to a full opinion if the risk is larger than it looked at triage.

control.basis: Four-eyes review within Risk on short-form notes

evidence.note: Shares estimated.

steps.name: Submit the opinion to the committee secretariat and file it
steps.description: The associate saves the final opinion or note in the memo repository, sends it to the Total Fund Management secretariat for the committee pre-read package, and records the conditions recommended so they can be followed after approval.

evidence.note: Committee materials are circulated before meetings; filing and conditions log are estimates.

steps.name: Brief the Head of Risk before the committee meeting
steps.description: The director briefs the Head of Risk, who sits on the Portfolio Execution Committee, on the opinion's main points and open issues so the risk view can be given at the meeting.

next.condition: deal terms change before the meeting

evidence.note: The Head of Risk gives the risk view at the committee (PEC is an ISRC subcommittee with risk-related matters); briefing time estimated.

steps.name: Update the opinion for changed deal terms
steps.description: When price, structure, leverage or partner terms change after the opinion, the senior associate reruns the affected analysis, revises the opinion and sends it back for director approval before the meeting.

evidence.note: Final bids and terms move late in an auction; share of updates estimated.

exceptions.name: Deal withdrawn or lost during review
exceptions.description: The deal team drops the deal or loses the auction while Risk is waiting for answers, and the review stops.

exceptions.name: Deal terms change after the draft
exceptions.description: The factual check or late bid negotiations change price, structure or leverage, and Risk reassesses before approval.

exceptions.name: Contested or limit-impacting opinion
exceptions.description: The view is not supportive, the deal takes a limit near its threshold, or the item goes to the Board committee, so the Head of Risk signs.

exceptions.name: Short-form item upgraded
exceptions.description: A routine item turns out larger or riskier than it looked at triage and is moved to the full opinion path.

exceptions.name: Terms change after the opinion is submitted
exceptions.description: The final bid or structure changes before the meeting and the opinion is updated and re-approved.

exceptions.name: Large deal needs a liquidity check
exceptions.description: Funding, unfunded commitments or guarantees are large enough that Total Fund Management confirms the liquidity and leverage impact.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from memo received by Risk to opinion delivered and Head of Risk briefed
benchmarks.population: Transactions submitted to the investment committee of a large Canadian pension investment manager

evidence.note: Estimate consistent with the committee workflow, where the secretariat waits about three days for the opinion after its own fit review, and with 4 to 6 week auction rounds that leave about a week for internal approvals.
Department contributions to one-year potential loss; the largest private contributors are where most opinions come from.

benchmarks.unit: share of total book value of assets in one person or associated persons
share of net assets, effective April 1, 2022

evidence.note: Board-level limit on Recourse Leverage.

pain_points.description: Memos reach Risk late in the deal timetable, so the analysis and approvals are compressed into a few days before the committee.

evidence.note: Auction rounds of 4 to 6 weeks leave little room; compression is an inference.

pain_points.description: Answers from deal teams wait behind bid work and are the longest single wait in a full review.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Private deals have to be mapped to public-market proxies to measure their risk contribution, and a poor proxy can understate risk.

evidence.note: Risk models and proxies are reviewed and updated (F2022); the mapping problem is an inference.

pain_points.description: Exposures to the same company or sector held through other departments or funds are hard to see in one place.

evidence.note: Committees organised by pod can miss portfolio-level concentration.

pain_points.description: Terms that change after the opinion force reruns and a second approval close to the meeting.

evidence.note: Estimate.

assumptions: The opinion is modelled as starting when Risk receives the draft memo; informal early engagement during diligence is not counted as a case.

The private equity senior associate role stands in for deal team members of every investment department who answer Risk's questions; their time is small and also appears in the departments' diligence workflows.
The 63% full and 37% short-form split, approval levels and rework shares are estimates; the organisation does not publish its Risk Policy or opinion thresholds.
Trigger shares copy the committee workflow's split of items by source so the two workflows agree.
The daily risk report is a standing input for exposures and limit use and does not start a case.

Risk roles sit in the organisation file's Risk unit; the process owner is the Investment risk oversight team of about 25 people, so the stated 7 FTE of Risk staff fits within that team alongside its other oversight work.
Loaded hourly costs come from the organisation file (overhead factor 1.25), which are far above Job Bank market medians because incentive pay is large.
